samuel2.1.p1.b1.text: After the death of Saul, David returned from the slaughter of the Amalekites and stayed in Ziklag two days.

samuel2.1.p1.b2.text: On the third day a man with torn clothes and dust on his head arrived from Saul’s camp. …

samuel2.1.p1.b3.text: … When he came to David, he fell to the ground to pay him homage.

samuel2.1.p2.b2.text: What was the outcome? … Please tell me.

samuel2.1.p2.b3.text: … And Saul and his son Jonathan are also dead.

samuel2.1.p2.b4.text: How do you know that Saul and his son Jonathan are dead?

samuel2.1.p3.b1.text: I happened to be on Mount Gilboa, … and there was Saul, leaning on his spear, with the chariots and the cavalry closing in on him.

samuel2.1.p3.b2.text: When he turned around and saw me, he called out

samuel2.1.p3.b3.text: Stand over me and kill me, for agony has seized me, but my life still lingers.

samuel2.1.p3.b4.text: … And I took the crown that was on his head and the band that was on his arm, and I have brought them here to my lord.

samuel2.1.p4.b1.text: Then David took hold of his own clothes and tore them, and all the men who were with him did the same.

samuel2.1.p4.b2.text: They mourned and wept and fasted until evening …

samuel2.1.p4.b3.text: … for Saul and his son Jonathan, and for the people of the LORD and the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.

samuel2.1.p5.b2.text: I am the son of a foreigner, … I am an Amalekite.

samuel2.1.p5.b3.text: Why were you not afraid to lift your hand to destroy the LORD’s anointed?

samuel2.1.p5.b4.text: Your blood be on your own head because your own mouth has testified against you, saying, ‘I killed the LORD’s anointed.’

samuel2.1.p6.b1.text: Then David took up this lament for Saul and his son Jonathan,

samuel2.1.p6.b2.text: … the Song of the Bow. It is written in the Book of Jashar

samuel2.1.p6.b3.text: “Your glory, O Israel, lies slain on your heights. How the mighty have fallen!

samuel2.1.p7.b1.text: Tell it not in Gath; proclaim it not in the streets of Ashkelon, …

samuel2.1.p7.b2.text: … lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, and the daughters of the uncircumcised exult.

samuel2.1.p7.b3.text: O mountains of Gilboa, may you have no dew or rain, no fields yielding offerings of grain.

samuel2.1.p7.b4.text: For there the shield of the mighty was defiled, the shield of Saul, no longer anointed with oil.

samuel2.1.p8.b1.text: From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, the bow of Jonathan did not retreat, and the sword of Saul did not return empty.

samuel2.1.p8.b2.text: Saul and Jonathan, beloved and delightful in life, were not divided in death. They were swifter than eagles, they were stronger than lions.

samuel2.1.p8.b3.text: O daughters of Israel, weep for Saul, who clothed you in scarlet and luxury, who decked your garments with ornaments of gold.

samuel2.1.p9.b1.text: How the mighty have fallen in the thick of battle! Jonathan lies slain on your heights.

samuel2.1.p9.b2.text: I grieve for you, Jonathan, my brother. You were delightful to me; your love to me was extraordinary, surpassing the love of women.

samuel2.1.p9.b3.text: How the mighty have fallen and the weapons of war have perished!”
